record.paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
record.original_question: Find usable sufficient conditions guaranteeing that a planar achievement set E(x_n, y_n) has nonempty interior.

evidence.quote: Find reasonable sufficient conditions for int E(xn, yn) ≠ ∅.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(x_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ and $(y_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be sequences of real numbers such that the series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} x_n$ and $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} y_n$ are absolutely convergent. Define the planar achievement set
$$E(x_n,y_n) = \left\{\left(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varepsilon_n x_n,\; \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varepsilon_n y_n\right) : (\varepsilon_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}} \in \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}\right\} \subset \mathbb{R}^2.$$
Find usable sufficient conditions on the pair of sequences $(x_n)$ and $(y_n)$ that guarantee that the topological interior of $E(x_n, y_n)$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$ is nonempty, i.e. $\operatorname{int} E(x_n, y_n) \neq \emptyset$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a recent survey on achievement sets. While there are partial results on the one-dimensional case (Kakeya-type theorems and conditions for E to be an interval or have nonempty interior), the planar analogue lacks a complete and usable interior criterion. Web search did not surface a published resolution.
